title: Sell Mineral Rights in Morris, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Morris, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own coalbed methane or mineral interests near Morris, AL along the Mulberry Fork? Get a straight, courthouse-researched offer, no pressure to sign anything.
heroLead: Morris sits along the Mulberry Fork of the Black Warrior River in the coal country of north Jefferson County, where the Mary Lee coal group has been mined and, later, degassed for methane for the better part of a century.
intro: Coal mining shaped Morris and the small communities strung along the Mulberry Fork long before anyone in Alabama talked about coalbed methane as its own commodity. Underground mines worked the Pottsville-age coal seams here for decades, and when operators later realized that same methane trapped in the coal could be produced as gas in its own right, a lot of this acreage got leased a second time — sometimes to a different company than the one that had mined it. That's left a fair number of Morris-area families holding an interest that was severed, leased, or partly produced under terms nobody currently living negotiated.

sections.heading: Coal Mining History, Then a Gas Lease
paragraphs: If your family's ground near Morris was ever part of an underground coal lease, there's a real chance the same coal seam later got leased separately for methane, since the gas and the coal were often owned and worked by different parties. Sorting out whether your interest is coal, gas, or both — and whether either lease is still active — is exactly the kind of title question we run down at the Jefferson County Courthouse before we make an offer.

sections.heading: What a Producing Well Nearby Tells Us
paragraphs: CBM wells in this part of the basin tend to produce water early and gas later, which makes the royalty history on a specific well more informative than any general area figure. If you're getting a check, even a small or irregular one, that record is the starting point for a fair number — we price against your actual statements, not a flat rate for north Jefferson County.

faqs.question: We think our minerals were leased for coal decades ago, not gas. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal — coal and coalbed methane are sometimes owned separately here. We check the courthouse record to see exactly what was conveyed before we quote a number.

faqs.question: Our royalty check from a Morris-area well is small and irregular. Is it even worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. CBM wells produce unevenly, especially early in dewatering. We look at the pattern over several months, not one check, before we price it.

faqs.question: How fast can this actually move?
faqs.answer: Once we've confirmed the title at the courthouse, most straightforward interests close within a few weeks. Complicated heir situations take longer, but we handle that research ourselves.
